name: Predicted-region multiplicative value gate
motivation: The preceding additive value-role pilot changed many frame logits but had negligible Dice effect. This candidate tests a distinct mechanism grounded in RMNet: mask-defined regions multiplicatively modulate memory values. The modulation is content-preserving at initialization and bounded so it cannot erase tokens.
method: For each of SAM2's four memory-attention layers, learn a per-channel multiplicative gain for each predicted foreground, mixed-boundary, or background value token. Initialize gains at 1 and bound them to [0.75, 1.25]. Keep queries, keys, attention probabilities, pointers, all tokens, memory writes, encoder, decoder, and frame schedule unchanged.

prior_work.adaptation: RMNet computes a mask-derived regional map and multiplies both memory keys and values by it. This SAM2 adaptation uses predicted-mask region assignments to learn bounded channel-wise multiplicative gains on spatial values only; it retains every SAM2 token and pointer and leaves native keys and attention scores unchanged.
prior_work.MMN_code_status: No official public repository was located during this survey; no MMN implementation is claimed.

model.initialization: Gain logits are zero, giving multiplicative gain exactly 1 and bit-identical native attention.

data.scope: Exploratory only: PolypGen informed earlier analyses and candidate design; patient-to-sequence independence is unverified.

training.loss: Mean author-compatible post-prompt decoder BCE plus Dice mask loss and object-presence loss across sampled clips.

evaluation.primary: Equal-sequence mean present-frame Dice over seq16-seq23.
evaluation.success_screen: At least +0.01 equal-sequence Dice over native, higher Dice on at least 6/8 sequences, and no increase in pooled false alarms on GT-empty frames.
evaluation.interpretation: One seed is a screening experiment, not reliable confirmation. A positive result requires a second pre-specified seed and an untouched external dataset before a general performance claim.
